name: How much space do I lose when converting a two-car garage?

mainEntity.name: If I convert a two-car garage into an ADU, how much usable living area and storage should I expect to gain or lose?
mainEntity.text: If I convert a two-car garage into an ADU, how much usable living area and storage should I expect to gain or lose?

acceptedAnswer.text: A two-car garage conversion rarely feels like a simple room swap. The usable living area depends on how much of the structure can be preserved, how the interior is framed, and how the kitchen and bathroom are arranged. You may end up with a comfortable studio or one-bedroom layout, but you also lose the garage’s original parking and storage functions. That tradeoff matters if the household still needs places for bikes, tools, seasonal items, or trash enclosures. Good ADU planning should account for those losses and include exterior storage, cabinets, or a small shed if allowed. Homeowners often underestimate how quickly square footage disappears once walls, insulation, mechanical chases, and code-required circulation are added. A designer should show the net usable area, not just the rough garage dimensions, so expectations are realistic.
acceptedAnswer.description: A two-car garage usually becomes a compact one-bedroom or large studio rather than a large apartment. You gain enclosed living space, but you lose vehicle storage, hobby space, and often some utility or storage functions unless the design includes built-ins or separate storage planning.
